title: Observability Fundamentals
description: Learn the fundamentals of observability and why it is critical for microservices.

data.text: Observability is the ability to understand the internal state of a system by examining its external outputs. Google, Netflix, and Uber invest heavily in observability because in microservices architectures, failures are common and debugging requires deep visibility.

data.title: Observability Pillars
items: Logs: Discrete events with context about what happened
Metrics: Numeric measurements over time (latency, error rate, throughput)
Traces: End-to-end request journeys across services

data.text: Monitoring tells you when something is wrong based on predefined metrics. Observability lets you explore and understand why something is wrong. In microservices, monitoring is not enough; you need observability to debug distributed systems.

data.title: Google's SRE Approach
data.text: Google's Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) team popularized observability. They use the three pillars to maintain services at massive scale, with golden signals (latency, traffic, errors, saturation) as their primary metrics.

data.title: Example: Golden Signals
data.code:
# Golden Signals

# Latency: Time to service requests
# - Track p50, p95, p99 latencies
# - Alert on latency degradation

# Traffic: Demand on your service
# - Requests per second
# - Bandwidth usage

# Errors: Rate of failed requests
# - 5xx errors per second
# - Failed authentication rate

# Saturation: Resource utilization
# - CPU, memory, disk, network
# - Connection pool usage
# - Thread pool saturation

data.caption: Three pillars of observability
data.definition:
graph TD
    O[Observability] --> L[Logs]
    O --> M[Metrics]
    O --> T[Traces]
    L -->|What happened| S[Service]
    M -->|How is it performing| S
    T -->|Request journey| S

items.question: Do I need all three pillars?
items.answer: Start with metrics and logs. Add distributed tracing when you need to debug request flows across services. All three complement each other.

items.question: What tools should I use?
items.answer: Popular stacks include: Prometheus + Grafana (metrics), ELK/Loki (logs), Jaeger/Zipkin (traces). OpenTelemetry is becoming the standard for all three.

items.question: How much observability is enough?
items.answer: Instrument your services thoroughly but avoid excessive logging that hurts performance. Focus on golden signals and request-level traces for critical paths.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Observability helps you understand why systems fail
Three pillars: logs, metrics, and traces
Start with golden signals for metrics
data.takeaway: Invest in observability early; debugging production microservices without it is nearly impossible.
